notes: §1985:XII.3.3 SR8: "If the word REPLACE appears in a comment-entry or in the place where a comment-entry may appear, it is considered part of the comment-entry." FixedFormConverter carries every line of an AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED or SECURITY paragraph (header and Area B lines) as a CommentEntryCarrier comment, FindStatementKeyword walks TextWordScanner words that skip comments, so no REPLACE there is a statement, and CommentEntryResolver.Resolve settles the entry after text manipulation. Witness: AUTHOR. REPLACE =="AAA"== BY =="BBB"==. leaves DISPLAY "AAA" (AAA). Probes (classes b, d): REPLACE in an Area B line of AUTHOR, lowercase replace in INSTALLATION, REPLACE in DATE-WRITTEN's next line, REPLACE OFF and a second REPLACE in DATE-COMPILED, an unclosed == in SECURITY (s8a: AAA); a REPLACE in Area A after the period ends the entry and is a statement (s8b: BBB); a REPLACE active before IDENTIFICATION DIVISION leaves AUTHOR's text alone and still replaces the procedure (s8c: ZZZ).

next.reason: 1985 makes the word REPLACE inside a comment-entry part of the comment-entry. 2023 has no comment-entries (the term and the AUTHOR/INSTALLATION/DATE-WRITTEN/DATE-COMPILED/SECURITY paragraphs do not occur in ISO 1989:2023); §2023:7.2.4.3 SR1 places REPLACE only where a character-string or separator may appear. No 2023 rule carries this requirement.
